title: Measurement: Pi's interactive /login in the full TUI, and what the same launch does without a TTY (Linux only)
summary: TSK-0065, toward ACC-0090. LINUX ONLY: every run is WSL Ubuntu 24.04 under script(1), which gives Pi a pseudo-terminal. Nothing here says how Pi behaves in a Windows terminal. WHAT PI OFFERS. Pi 0.84.4 has no authentication-only launch (F7). `pi auth` offers only check, print-api-key and print-bearer-token, and /login exists only as a slash command inside the interactive TUI. The check therefore launches the full TUI. THE LAUNCH, FIXED FOR EVERY RUN. The pinned CLI from a clean clone at 061a706, with --no-session --no-extensions --no-skills --no-prompt-templates --no-themes --no-context-files --no-approve --offline, an environment of exactly HOME, LANG, PATH, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and TERM, and HOME, the agent directory and the working directory each a fresh temporary directory. PATH holds Node's directory and the system binaries only. THE NO-TTY CONTROLS. The same launch, with stdin and stdout varied, each stopped at 20 s by timeout, with Pi's exit and elapsed time taken inside the Pi stage. With both streams a terminal, the TUI rendered and was still running at the timeout (exit 124, 20.1 s). This is the mode control: it shows the probe sees the TUI when it is there. With stdin /dev/null, Pi exited 0 in 0.3 s and printed nothing. With stdout a pipe, Pi exited 0 in 0.2 s and printed nothing. With stdin an open pipe, and with both streams pipes, Pi was still running at the timeout (exit 124). In none of the four did the TUI render. Those runs are not the interactive mode. That Pi selected print mode in them is read from its source (resolveAppMode in dist/main.js) and agrees with what was observed, and the waiting runs agree with Pi reading an open stdin pipe until it closes (F8). No no-TTY case refused: two exited 0 silently, and two waited until stopped. THE INTERACTIVE RUN. An operator at a real terminal typed /login, chose Sign in with an API key, selected OpenAI and pasted a throwaway key generated by the harness, which works nowhere. Pi reported 'Saved API key for OpenAI', and the operator exited. Pi exited 0 after 36.8 s. The TUI rendered, and Pi read the operator's keystrokes while the harness read nothing from stdin. AUTH, ASKED SEPARATELY. Before the run, pi auth check --provider openai --json --no-refresh exited 1 with not_ready and credentials_not_configured. After it, the same check exited 0 with ready, openai, api_key. The isolated auth.json held one openai entry of type api_key, and it held the key that was entered. This confirms locally configured authentication. It does not show the key works against OpenAI, and account authentication belongs to TSK-0066. F13: PI DISPLAYS THE KEY. The key prompt shows the pasted key in plain text, unmasked, and the transcript captured it on every redraw. It appeared three times: twice in the key prompt, and once where the operator first pasted it into the provider search box. Anything that logs or tees the terminal during /login records the key. F14: A SESSION MODEL WAS SELECTED. After saving, Pi printed 'Selected gpt-5.5' and the status line changed from unknown to gpt-5.5. This run did not compare Pi's settings before and after, so it does not establish whether that selection was persisted. F15: the success message prints the absolute path of the credentials file. KEY ABSENCE. The harness generated the key, removed every occurrence from the transcript, and refused to save the record or the transcript if any 8-character run of the key's random part survived. Both were saved, so neither held one. The key and any fingerprint of it were discarded with the run. test/pi-compat-login.test.mjs cannot know the key, so it does not prove its absence. It checks the pin, the launch arguments, the environment names, each control's mode and bounded outcome, the interactive exit, auth before and after, the stored shape, the redaction scan on all four files, that no hex run of 16 or more survives, and that the transcript's redaction markers match the recorded redaction count. Four altered copies of the records each failed it, and the files were restored byte-identical by sha256.

facts.platform: WSL Ubuntu 24.04, Linux only, under script(1) from util-linux 2.39.3
facts.pi-version: 0.84.4, the pin, from a clean clone at 061a706 with npm ci
facts.environment-names: HOME, LANG, PATH, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, TERM; PATH is Node's directory plus /usr/bin:/bin
facts.isolation: HOME, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and the working directory are fresh temporary directories
facts.control-both-tty: TUI rendered; still running at the 20 s timeout, exit 124, 20.1 s
facts.control-stdin-closed: no TUI; exit 0 in 0.3 s; no output
facts.control-stdout-pipe: no TUI; exit 0 in 0.2 s; no output
facts.control-stdin-open-pipe: no TUI; still running at the 20 s timeout, exit 124
facts.control-both-pipes: no TUI; still running at the 20 s timeout, exit 124
facts.mode-attribution: print mode in the no-TTY rows is read from Pi's source (resolveAppMode) and agrees with the observed absence of the TUI; it is not observed directly
facts.interactive-exit: Pi exit 0 after 36.8 s; script exit 0
facts.terminal-ownership: the TUI rendered (bracketed paste enabled, cursor hidden, no alternate screen) and read the operator's keystrokes; the harness read nothing from stdin during the run
facts.auth-before: pi auth check --provider openai --json --no-refresh: exit 1, not_ready, credentials_not_configured
facts.auth-after: the same check: exit 0, ready, openai, api_key
facts.stored: auth.json held one openai entry of type api_key, and it was the entered key; compared at capture and reduced to a boolean
facts.f13-key-displayed: Pi displays the pasted key in plain text; three occurrences were redacted from the transcript, two in the key prompt and one in the provider search box
facts.f14-model-selected: Pi printed 'Selected gpt-5.5' and the status line changed to gpt-5.5; whether this was persisted is not established by this run
facts.f15-path-printed: the success message prints the absolute credentials path
facts.key-absence: enforced at capture time by login-check.mjs, which refuses to save if any 8-character run of the key's random part survives; the key and any fingerprint of it were not retained
facts.test-sensitivity: four altered record copies each failed it; restored byte-identical by sha256
facts.transcript-normalisation: after capture, trailing spaces on each line (the TUI pads lines to the terminal width) and blank lines at the end of each file were removed from both retained transcripts; the harness now does the same at capture. Nothing else was changed, and the redaction-marker count still matches the record

omissions.reason: Every run is Linux under script(1). Windows terminal behaviour is not inferred from it.
The key is a throwaway, and the auth check ran with --no-refresh. Account authentication is TSK-0066's.
Only the API-key route was exercised. Subscription OAuth is TSK-0066's.
Pi's settings were not compared before and after the run, so whether 'Selected gpt-5.5' was persisted is unknown.
The retained test cannot know the generated key. The absence claim rests on the capture-time check.
The checks need script(1) and, for the interactive half, a person at a terminal, so they run manually. The retained test runs in the default suite and has not run in CI yet.
